NERVES. [36] [Apis]
Nervous irritability ; restless, agitated. θ Hydrocephalus. θ Diphtheria. θ Scarlatina.
Irritability and uneasiness.
Nervous excitability. θ Apyrexia in intermittent.
Hysteria.
Nervous erethism.
Nervous restlessness at night, cannot remain in one place.
Restless, with cutaneous diseases.
Great restlessness and uneasiness. θ Scarlatina.
Great uneasiness and yawning. θ Intermittent.
Trembling and jerking of limbs. θ Hydrocephalus. θ Typhus.
Trembling, with lassitude.
Weakness, with trembling.
A single involuntary jerk frequently repeated.
Sudden jerks through joints and other parts.
One-half of body twitching, the other lame. θ Tubercular meningitis. θ Hydrocephalus.
Sudden convulsions, followed by general fever. θ Meningitis infantum.
Convulsions. θ Hydrocephalus. θ Scarlatina. θ Tubercular meningitis.
Eclampsia, with inflammatory affection of brain.
Hysteric convulsions.
Faint, pale and cold, with vomiting and diarrhœa.
Faint, uneasy, restless, yawning. θ Uterine hemorrhage.
Sudden weakness, compelling him to lie down ; he loses all recollection.
Frequent loss of all strength, with a trembling sensation.
Very weak, must lie down.
Great weakness of all limbs. θ Trichinosa.
So weak that she could only with difficulty stand on her feet. θ Ovarian dropsy.
Greatest weakness on sliding down in bed. θ Typhus.
Weak and pale. θ Scarlatina. θ Ascites.
Amazing weariness.
Tired, as if bruised in every limb.
Weariness, with debility in Spring, after least effort, with paroxysm of vertigo, paleness and chilliness.
Great debility as if he had worked hard ; he is obliged to lie down.
Great debility from the beginning. θ Diphtheria.
Great debility. θ Chronic dysentery. θ Intermittent, apyrexia. θ Ascites.
General feeling of lassitude and depression.
Lassitude ; indisposition to mental or physical exertion. θ Bilious diarrhœa.
Languid, listless, unaccountable feeling. θ Diarrhœa.
General feeling of lassitude, with trembling.
Greatest lassitude and languor. θ Incipient hydrocephalus.
Great prostration. θ Peritonitis. θ Eruptive diseases.
Prostration : peculiar ; as from within ; great, for several days ; general, particularly in cold weather ; sudden, with coldness.
Tendency to chilliness, and a quite peculiar prostration of vital force of nerve centres. θ Chest complaints.
Prostration and lassitude. θ Dropsy.
Great exhaustion, after all symptoms pass away.
Fell down and declared he was dying. θ After stings.
Anticipation of sudden death. θ Peritonitis.
Paralysis generally one-sided, often painful.
After excessive grief the whole right side paralyzed.
White puffy swelling of paralyzed arm and hand.
Whole nervous system under a paralyzing influence. θ Scarlatina.
Sudden, right-sided paralysis.
Partial paralysis of right side, with numbness. θ Cancer of breast.
Left side motionless ; now and then moves right arm and leg. θ Tubercular meningitis. θ Hydrocephalus.
   

SLEEP. [37] [Apis]
Yawning.
Yawning and great uneasiness. θ Uterine hemorrhage.
Yawning and great desire to sleep.
Sleepiness more after meals.
Great inclination to sleep ; still he walks a tenth of a German mile.
Inclined to sleep. θ Acute Bright's disease. θ Incipient hydrocephalus. θ Keratitis. θ Intermittent, etc.
Great inclination to sleep, but inability to do so from great nervous restlessness.
In daytime always sleepy, in a dull, stupid state ; at night talking in her sleep, which was full of dreams ; towards morning sleep so profound that she had to be shaken to awake her. θ Sopor.
Great desire to sleep, he felt extremely drowsy.
Very sleepy early in evening.
Sleepiness, prostration and vomiting of bile.
Continuous deep sleep. θ Hot stage of intermittent fever.
Somnolence.
Sopor, with eruptive diseases.
Stupor ; when shaken, looking about strangely. θ Typhus.
Lies flat down in a stupor ; even shaking does not bring him to consciousness. θ Typhus.
Sleepless, mostly latter part of night.
Restless sleep ; child restless, fretful, sleepless, hot. θ Abscess after vaccination.
Cough prevents sleep. θ Typhus.
Restless nights. θ Hydrocephalus. θ Bilious diarrhœa.
Restless, sleepless. θ Erysipelas. θ Ovarian tumor.
Tension in face, shooting in skin, burning pain under l. ribs, or other ailments prevent sleep.
Frequent waking.
Disturbed sleep. θ Scarlatina.
Wakefulness. θ Hydrocephalus. θ Intermittent.
Sleeplessness, with eruptive diseases.
No sleep for days.
Restless sleep and incessant dreaming.
Night sleep full of dreams ; mostly of traveling.
Sleep restless, frequent waking, incoherent dreaming.
Anxious dreams.
Sleep disturbed by oppressed respiration and disagreeable dreams.
Disturbed sleep at night ; dreams. θ Gastro-enteritis.
Dreams : of journeying ; of flying ; walking on a hot floor ; of assembled people ; full of care and trouble.
Sleep disturbed by oppression of breathing ; by incoherent muttering.
Sleep disturbed at night by muttering and dreams. θ Gastro-enteritis.
Disturbed sleep, with muttering and incoherent talking. θ Bronchitis.
Nights restless, without sleep, constantly delirious. θ Typhus.
At night talking in sleep, dreamy state. θ Incipient hydrocephalus.
Starting out of sleep.
Anxious starting in sleep. θ With cough.
Suddenly starts from sleep with great anxiety and agitation.
All night delirious, furibund. θ Typhus.
Trembling, convulsive starting during sleep, as if in affright.
Frequent waking at night with violent screams.
Awakens from sleep with a shrill shriek. θ Meningitis infantum.
Screaming in sleep ; "cri encephalique."
Sopor while lying in bed interrupted by sudden cries. θ Meningitis infantum.
The child is restless, screams out in sleep. θ Constipation of sucklings.
Agitation latter part of night. θ Incipient hydrocephalus.
Short sleep.
Long morning sleep.
Sleep in morning profound, cannot be waked without being taken out of bed, shaken and forced about for a time ; girl, æt. 8. θ Incipient hydrocephalus.
Wakes from sleep in morning weary and unrefreshed.
   

TIME. [38] [Apis]
Night : nursing child refuses milk, not so in daytime ; squinting, trembling of eyeball ; stitches in and around eye ; difficult breathing in laryngitis ; cough ; strangling ; feet swollen and stiff ; restless, dreaming ; sleepless in erysipelas, can see better than in daytime ; irritation of urinary organs < ; frequent urination.
Nocturnal sufferings, besides those dependent on sleep, are most in eye and chest.
At 9 P. M. to 4 A. M. : incessant cough.
Latter part of night : sleepless.
Towards night : increase of weariness, copious nosebleed, rigor, headache, mucus in mouth, bellyache, urging to stool and heartburn.
Always < towards morning. θ Dropsy.
At 5 A. M. : heat and fever followed by shaking chill.
Morning : aching at umbilicus ; diarrhœa < ; hoarseness ; sleeps till late ; dry coryza, bellyache with call to stool.
In morning less disturbed ; weakened consciousness. θ Typhus.
Day : stupid state in tubercular meningitis ; vomiting.
Day and night : must urinate every half hour.
At 3 to 4 P. M. : chill.
At 4 P. M. : sudden coryza.
Afternoon : fever, intermittent.
Evening : tip of nose cold, with chilliness ; pain in coccygeal region < ; chill < ; fluent coryza ; very sleepy.
Evening ; suffering and vertigo, headache, pain in eyes, toothache ; bellyache ; hoarseness, but most cough, shivering and heat.
Before midnight : cough awakens.
Before going to bed in evening a hard shivering fit. θ Chronic rheumatism.
Spring : spells of vertigo.
Fall : hives <.
   

TEMPERATURE AND WEATHER. [39] [Apis]
Heat of stove increases chill.
Warm room : headaches < ; breathing in laryngitis and ascites < ; chill <.
Heated room intolerable.
Warmth of bed : rash with itching < ; breathing in laryngitis <.
In-doors : sweat is increased.
Open air, out-of-doors : relieves headache ; difficult respiration ; rash with itching.
Inclination for open air.
Shunning cold air.
Uncovering relieves heat.
Cold water relieves eyelids (applied locally).
Worse getting wet through, but better from washing or moistening part in cold water.
Cold water relieves pains, swelling and burning.
Cold water, desire for washing face.
Cold weather : increases asthma ; cough ; pain in chest ; rash with itching ; prostration.
Changing weather increases rash with itching.
Spring : spells of vertigo ; prostration.
North wind : takes cold.
   

FEVER. [40] [Apis]
Disposed to chilliness.
Chilliness. θ Acute Bright's disease.
Felt very cold, but was not cold to touch.
Chill on suffering part.
Chill increased by motion.
Chill, 3 to 4 P. M., < in warm room or near stove ; begins in front of chest ; thirst during chill, burning and oppression of chest as if he would smother. θ Intermittent.
Chill, mostly towards evening, 3 to 4 P. M.
Chill increased in warm room.
Evening before going to bed a hard shivering fit. θ Rheumatism.
Always thirst during chill.
Shivering on slightest movement when sitting in evening, with headache, heat of face, hot hands.
Chilly every P. M. at 3 o'clock ; she shudders, < in warmth ; chills run down back ; hands feel as if dead ; feverishly hot after about an hour, with a hoarse cough ; heat of cheeks and hands, without thirst ; ceases gradually, but she feels heavy and prostrate.
Shivering followed by heat. θ Tonsillitis.
Slight rigors followed by flushes of heat over entire body, with headache, weariness in back and legs.
Severe chill, evening, following an operation lasting three hours ; followed by high fever with great vascular excitement ; the wound erysipelatous. θ Erysipelas traumatica.
A shaking chill followed by great heat, during which whole lower limb swelled more and more, and pains in it became insupportable. θ Thrombosis.
Pungent heat of body while feet and hands are cold.
Hot head, cold feet. θ Ophthalmia.
After heat, rigor with an eruption of nettlerash.
With general heat, feeling of chilliness in feet and legs up to knee. θ Typhus.
Increasing heat and fever for thirty-six hours, followed by severe shaking chill, 5 A. M.
Skin burning hot all over, or gradually grows cool in some places, hot in others.
Heat in some parts, coldness in others.
Febrile excitement. θ Heart disease.
Flushes of heat over whole surface of body.
Great fever heat. θ Hydrocephalus.
High fever. θ Phlegmasia.
Fever rises continually. θ Scarlatina.
Burning heat of skin with a stinging sensation. θ Ovarian dropsy.
Dry burning skin. θ Typhus.
Little febrile excitement or other constitutional symptoms, only in a few instances considerable. θ Erysipelas.
Burning heat all over.
Dry skin, no sweat. θ Mania.
Dry heat towards evening, with sleepiness.
Feverish heat during night, other times pale. θ Chronic diarrhœa.
Heat most about chest, belly and hands. θ Intermittent.
Heat most in chest, pit of stomach, bowels, female organs and hands, with muttering and unconsciousness. θ Intermittent.
Hot feeling all over body, especially on chest and in region of stomach.
During heat : delirium, muttering unconsciousness ; diarrhœa ; short-breathed ; drowsy or sleepless.
During hot stage more or less violent headache, generally a continuous deep sleep. θ Intermittent.
Got hot all over, red in face as if he had scarlet fever, with an eruption like measles (after overdoses). θ Chronic diarrhœa.
Most violent fever, with a puffed, darkened face, eyes shooting, shining, with a wild, obstinate expression and unbearable headache. θ Typhus.
Thirst wanting during sweat ; may or may not be present during heat.
Fever without thirst.
Heat, with (or without) thirst and inclination to uncover.
Fever constantly rising ; dry hot skin. θ Scarlatina.
Violent fever, with dry skin, full pulse. θ Bronchitis.
High fever, full pulse. θ Incipient hydrocephalus.
Fever, with rapid, hard pulse ; exacerbation during evening.
Heat, inclined to uncover, which is agreeable ; rapid, hard pulse ; after fever spell, sleep.
Heavy and prostrate in fever.
Whole surface glowing, hot, skin dry, brittle. θ Typhus.
Heat, redness and extreme soreness. θ Erysipelas.
Heat, with redness of skin ; in evening and night ; with excitement, headache, accompanying diarrhœa, swellings, coughs.
Dry hot skin, or alternate dry and moist skin.
Skin hot, moist. θ Diphtheria. θ Catarrh of chest.
High fever, moist skin. θ Diphtheria.
Sweat alternating with dryness of skin.
Alternate moisture and dryness of skin. θ Intermittent.
Dryness of skin, very little sweat. θ Intermittent.
Sweating stage either absent or of a very light grade. θ Intermittent.
Sweats easily.
Cold sweat. θ Dropsy after scarlatina.
General warm sweat during recovery from effects of an indescribably bad odor, causing physician a dull ache in forehead lasting several hours, until Apis[6] removed it. θ Typhus.
Partial clammy sweats. θ Typhus.
Profuse sweat relieves rheumatism.
Thirst wanting during sweat ; may or may not be present during heat ; always thirst during chill.
Sweat after trembling and fainting, then nettlerash.
Better after sweating ; sweat increased in-doors.
Headache and sleeplessness ; skin warm ; profuse sweat on the fourth day and relief. θ Rheumatism.
Chills and fever in seasons when flies sting with unusual vigor.
Low, muttering delirium ; sometimes a happy expression ; apathy ; stupor ; cannot put tongue out ; tongue trembles, catches in teeth, or is cracked, sore and covered with blisters ; abdomen sore, bloated, stool frequent, painful, foul, bloody, often involuntary. θ Typhus.
Typhoid forms of fever, especially enteric, cerebral, exanthematic forms ; febris nervosa putrida.
Typhoid character of fever in scarlatina.
Intermittent. A very important antipyretic (in one of the most malarial countries) given according to Wolf in the third centesimal, but for two years the one hundredth centesimal potency ; they have seen results, such as they had not for many years witnessed from any other homeopathic remedy against intermittent fever, at least as regards the rapidity of the result. (Drs. Stern and Miskolez).
Tertian intermittent.
Since a year, sixty-five intermittent cases of various age and sex ; nineteen among these had been suppressed by large doses of quinine, etc. No relapse.
Apyrexia : pain under short ribs, left side ; feet swollen ; urine scanty ; limbs and joints sore ; restless ; urticaria.
